recognize_zh: 右上方大紅血球內有單一、圓形、深紫色、邊界清楚的小體（Howell-Jolly 小體）；中央的大紅血球內則是數個更小、不規則的藍色顆粒（Pappenheimer 小體），可在同一視野比較兩者差異，背景有明顯大小不一與變形紅血球。
features: Single round, dense, dark purple inclusion near the edge of a macrocytic red cell (upper right) = Howell-Jolly body
Central macrocyte with a few small, irregular basophilic granules = Pappenheimer bodies
Marked anisopoikilocytosis: macrocytes, microcytes, teardrop cell, ovalocytes, irregular/crenated cells and a target-like cell
Variably sized platelets scattered in the background
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows marked anisopoikilocytosis with macrocytes, microcytes, a teardrop cell, ovalocytes, target-like and irregularly contoured red cells. A macrocyte at the upper right contains a single round, dense, dark purple Howell-Jolly body, and the large red cell in the center contains several small irregular basophilic granules consistent with Pappenheimer bodies. Platelets are present. The combination of Howell-Jolly and Pappenheimer bodies suggests hyposplenism or asplenia, possibly with an underlying dyserythropoietic or sideroblastic process; a Prussian blue stain can confirm the iron content of the Pappenheimer bodies.

ddx.vs: Pappenheimer bodies are smaller, multiple, irregular and Prussian blue-positive, whereas the Howell-Jolly body is single, round, larger and Feulgen (DNA)-positive.
A platelet on top of a red cell has granular texture with a pale blue periphery rather than a homogeneous dense round inclusion.
A ring has a blue cytoplasmic loop attached to the chromatin dot, not a solitary solid dot.
Precipitate is refractile, lies in a different focal plane and is also found between cells.
